subject: error matrix representation in lavaan in a cfa model

messages.author: 7636027d6c15836f
messages.subject: error matrix representation in lavaan in a cfa model
parts:
given a CFA model in its general form y=Λη+ε
where
Λ is the loading representation matrix
η is the factor loading matrix
and most importantly
ε is a mxm matrix where m=number of items and it represents errors. its diagonal represent unique errors and the off diagonal elements represent error correlation/covariance between items.

The question is:
is there any way to use matrix representation of the model for estimation instead of using lavaan syntax to estimate the parameters of the model?

i.e. say I have a model representation in matrix notation is there any way to use these matrices directly instead of using lavaan syntax to represent the model?

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: error matrix representation in lavaan in a cfa model
parts:
I do not believe there is a method of using matrix notation built into lavaan. The simsem package provides a method of using LISREL matrix notation to fit models with lavaan (see the first part of this page for an example: https://github.com/simsem/simsem/wiki/Example-7:-Analyzing-Real-Data-and-then-Run-Monte-Carlo-Simulation) and I believe the RAMpath package provides a method of using RAM notation to fit models via lavaan.

Alex
